meetings.headline: PACC voted to keep its membership at five and heard a dispute over the PACC budget's expected income.
meetings.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee approved prior minutes, heard the manager's report on a budget-income dispute with the town accountant, and reviewed its section of the town bylaws. It voted to keep membership at five. It also discussed a streaming franchise fee bill, an HD channel charge, sports cameras, the Owl camera and copyright.

minutes.headline: PACC voted to keep its membership at five and heard a dispute over the PACC budget's expected income.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee approved prior minutes, heard the manager's report on a budget-income dispute with the town accountant, and reviewed its section of the town bylaws. It voted to keep membership at five. It also discussed a streaming franchise fee bill, an HD channel charge, sports cameras, the Owl camera and copyright.

public_comment.topic: A visitor said they were there on invitation to learn.

votes.motion: Keep the committee at five members in the bylaws

budget_items.what_was_said: The manager said the accountant told the committee it could budget only expected income because rent was not yet qualified. The town warrant showed a higher amount, and the committee had not seen those numbers before they appeared on screen.
Capital equipment funds did not appear on the financial report until used.
Rent was paid this month, equipment and supplies were slightly up, and videographer payroll rose. Interest was received.
A side letter lets the cable company charge for HD equipment against the franchise fee. Members worried it could recur yearly across three channels.
A bill would set a statewide fee split among the state, the municipality and community media centers.
Sports camera systems are sold with tiered streaming subscriptions, with prices varying by sport and storage level.
The Owl camera was described as costing thousands, with a higher figure also mentioned.

decisions.decision: The handbook stays on the agenda, with a member asked to bring an outline.
The manager to confirm whether the select board sent the streaming letter.
No purchase of an Owl camera for now; it is to be kept in mind.
Bylaw committee recommendations are to be updated through about February ahead of town meeting.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to keep its membership at five in the town bylaws, though the minutes could not make the vote count audible.
The manager reported that the town accountant told the committee it could budget only expected income because rent was not yet qualified.
The town warrant showed a higher income amount than the committee had budgeted, and members had not seen those numbers before they appeared on screen.
Members heard that a side letter lets the cable company charge for HD equipment against the franchise fee, and worried it could recur yearly.
The committee decided not to buy an Owl meeting camera for now and to keep it in mind.

why_it_matters: The committee's budget depends on how much rent income the town accountant allows it to count, and that affects what the town's cable access operation can plan to spend.

The franchise fee, the HD equipment charge and the proposed state streaming fee each change how much cable-related money reaches local community media, which residents may see in what the channels can afford to cover.
watch_next: The bylaw committee's recommendations are to be updated through about February, ahead of town meeting, where any change to the committee's bylaw section would be voted.
The manager is to confirm whether the select board sent the letter on the proposed streaming franchise fee.
